correctness.rationale: Direct kernel beta integration and a central-binomial convolution give the exact Hilbert–Schmidt energy. Bin-integral moments prove all nonzero falling-factorial eigenvalues. A uniform cutoff log-product expansion and half-line Euler–Maclaurin give the squared-eigenvalue expansion to an order-\(1/n\) error; Stirling subtraction yields \(\Delta_n=1/6-5\sqrt\pi/(96\sqrt{n+1})+O(n^{-1})\). Finite-rank Schur decomposition plus kernel asymmetry proves positivity. The standalone rational and numerical checker passed 95 checks; infinite asymptotics rely on the analytic Gaussian error estimate.

value.rationale: \(\Delta_n\) measures the natural Schatten-two energy unexplained by the algebraic spectrum of a concrete nonnormal positive approximating operator; it is the squared Schur off-diagonal energy (plus input-space leakage). The nonzero exact limit 1/6 and its first correction reveal that strong convergence to identity and vanishing relative error do not eliminate this absolute defect. The quantity is motivated by spectral approximations and comparison of kernel singular energy with polynomial eigenmodes, not an arbitrary subset or a renamed general theorem.
